script: My hands cramp, I am trapped… but the doctor's secret will blow everything.. I had to write a 50‑minute English essay on paper, so my grandma dragged the laptop out of my hands and set a stack of lined sheets on the desk. I was like, "Fine, I'll do it." She was all, "You're a slow‑puncher, you're wasting time." (I know, right?) I started, my pen gliding, not a single worry. I was faster than usual, because why not? Then my hand began to cramp. I told her, "Bruh, my hand's hurting." She just huffed, "Stop being a hypochondriac and get on with it." (Literally insane.) I kept writing. Two minutes later my fingers locked like a rusty gate. Eight minutes of agony, but I kept my mouth shut so my plan—getting that paragraph done—could stay on track. The cramp came back, and again. Three full attacks before the timer hit zero. When I finished, I had one eight‑line paragraph, about 130 words. Grandma was not happy. She accused me of slowing down on purpose to piss her off. I tried to explain, but she wouldn't listen. Finally, she let me switch back to my laptop. I typed three solid paragraphs plus a conclusion in the same 50 minutes, using one hand. I've been dealing with these hand cramps for 4‑5 years. I am a 16‑year‑old, biologically male (but I identify as non‑binary, FYI). I can't write long enough for school or exams without the pain. I've learned to type with one hand to avoid the cramps, but grandma thinks I am lazy. I am not. I am just doing what's medically possible. I am going to book an appointment for my hand soon, because this isn't just about being "slow." It's about real pain and real limits.
